name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 389 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 389 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Manipur seized a Kuki-Zo camp, arrested 17 suspected militants and confiscated 24 firearms, while also taking control of the Sinai camp. In Kashmir, IGP Sujit Kumar reviewed crime disposal, winter preparedness and policing measures across the valley, and a youth was wounded in a bear attack in South Kashmir. The Kuki-Zo Women’s Forum called for President's Rule in Manipur, framing the crisis as political rather than security related, and Gaurav Gogoi questioned the Centre's response. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur tok kontroll over en Kuki-Zo-leir, arresterte 17 mistenkte militante og konfiskerte 24 skytevåpen, samtidig som de tok kontroll over Sinai-leiren. I Kashmir gjennomgikk IGP Sujit Kumar kriminalbehandlingen, vinterberedskapen og polititiltakene i dalen, og en ungdom ble såret i et bjørnangrep i Sør-Kashmir. Kuki-Zo-kvinnesamfunnet krevde presidentstyre i Manipur og fremstiller krisen som politisk snarere enn sikkerhetsrelatert, og Gaurav Gogoi stilte spørsmål ved sentralstyrets respons. 437 dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
